correctness.rationale: The causal factorization C_t=D(I−tS)^−1 proves compactness; pointwise order on positive matrices gives increasing norms (strict for 0<t<1, by testing on a nonnegative compact norm maximizer). In the inverse quotient, expanding the zero-extended difference squares gives t times the free gradient energy plus (1−t)^2 times the unweighted mass. The ground-state substitution v_n=sqrt(n+1)f_n gives conductance sqrt(n(n+1)) and diagonal Hardy excess (n+1)r_n, with r_0=7/4−sqrt(2)>0 and r_n nonnegative and of order (n+1)^−4 for n>=1. The sine test on the shortened logarithmic interval has mass a/2+O(1), gradient energy at most π²/(2a)+O(a^−2), summable Hardy excess O(a^−2), and exponentially small confining term. For the liminf, normalize discrete mass to L; O(1/L) excess gives vanishing f_0, bounded local H^1 of the interpolant at x_n=log(n+1)/L, and exponentially small mass on x>=1+δ for every δ>0. The mass comparison on [0,R] is with the sum truncated to x_n<=R: replacing 1/(n+1) by log((n+2)/(n+1)) costs O(1)/L on compacts, and max mesh width is O(1/L). For R>1, the tail bound recovers the full discrete mass. Thus the normalized limit lies in H_0^1(0,1), and on intervals away from zero the conductance tends to the continuum coefficient one. Sharp Dirichlet Poincaré yields π² in the reciprocal-squared norm gap, and differentiation of E^−1/2 at E=1/4 gives the stated 4π². The independent finite-section sandwich under originality also proves the main limit without this mesh argument. Read VERIFICATION.md and check.py; did not execute the uploaded code.

evidence: Put δ=1−t, L=log(1/δ), m_−=floor(δ^−1L^−4), m_+=ceil(δ^−1L^4). The leading m_− block dominates t^{m_−}A_{m_−} entrywise, hence ||C_t||>=t^{m_−}||A_{m_−}||. The rows through m_+ use no later columns and are dominated by A_{m_+}; remaining rows have norm at most ||(I−P_{m_+})D||||(I−tS)^−1||<=1/((m_++1)δ). Thus ||C_t||<=||A_{m_+}||+1/((m_++1)δ).
The additive tail and the lower multiplicative loss are O(L^−4), and log m_±/L→1. Applying the same prior asymptotic on both sides gives exactly the frozen 4π².

evidence: For the m by m unit-weight triangular Cesàro matrix A_m, Gao's μ_m is the squared 2→2 norm, since the matrix is nonnegative and absolute values suffice. With λ_k=1, Λ_k=k, L in Gao's hypotheses equals 1 and (1.8) reduces at p=2 to k/(k+1)<=1; the other weight conditions are immediate. With p=q=2 the formula gives μ_m=4−16π²/log²m+O(log^−3 m).
